name: Tiger Data (formerly Timescale, Inc.)
origin_detail: Founded in New York around 2015 by Ajay Kulkarni and Michael Freedman (a Princeton computer science professor), first as an IoT data platform (iobeam). It released TimescaleDB, a PostgreSQL extension, in 2017. The task brief records the later rename to Tiger Data; its date was not verified.
openness_notes: TimescaleDB launched under Apache-2.0. From late 2018 its advanced features were placed under the source-available Timescale License (TSL), which bars offering them as a hosted service, while the core stayed Apache-2.0: open core (2). Built on PostgreSQL, a community-governed project.

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 core + Timescale License (TSL) for advanced features

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Partial: the core stayed Apache-2.0; aimed at managed-Postgres resale; no significant fork known (unverified)

robustness: Depends on PostgreSQL, a foundation-like community project, which lowers lock-in; the company itself is single-vendor and VC-backed.
openness_effect_assessment: Not assessed: no sourced research was possible in this session.
key_takeaway: Draft only. Timescale built on PostgreSQL rather than its own engine, tying itself to a community-governed core, and split its licence in 2018 to target cloud resale without closing the core. Funding, valuation and the Tiger Data rebrand date need sourcing.
